## Biography

Lya hates space. She said so herself. Hermine Delarue rolled her eyes when Jasmina Halsey suggested consulting her.

Yet Lya is the expedition's lead astrophysicist. The contradiction makes sense once you understand her: she does not love the void, she maps it. She established the Orion observation post despite what Ram Tah called "a heart attack" — actually an instrument calibration failure. She back-traced the damaged DSSA beacon's trajectory to permit-locked systems in Praei2. She constructed the map that guided the search and rescue detachment to the derelict prototype. When theory and practice collided, Lya chose theory. "Space is big," Halsey said, defending her. "We need to narrow our focus." Lya narrowed it. From millions of cubic light-years to a single drifting hull. Not bad for someone who would rather be anywhere else.
